resources.string: Choose the page to show. To open settings later, tap the top-right corner five times within five seconds. A PIN is optional.
Enter an http:// or https:// address

Without a PIN, anyone who knows the corner gesture can change settings and exit. For public kiosks, keep PIN protection on and set up managed lockdown in settings. Ordinary installs can still be exited using Android\'s system controls.
Too many wrong PINs. Try again in %1$d s.
Ask for the PIN before opening settings or trusting a certificate
The corner gesture opens settings without a PIN
Anyone who knows the corner gesture will be able to change settings and exit, including in managed lockdown. Certificate trust decisions will also be possible without a PIN.
PIN protection is on but the saved PIN is missing. Restore the app settings or clear app storage to set up again.
Blocks Home, Recents and system controls while the kiosk is running. Takes effect when you return to the dashboard.
Requires Device Owner setup or approval from your device management provider

Managed lockdown keeps visitors inside dKiosk using Android's lock task mode. PIN protection is separate and optional. Without a PIN, the corner gesture permits administrator access and exit.

For a dedicated device, back up its data and provision dKiosk as Device Owner before adding accounts. This usually requires a factory reset; installing the app or granting ordinary device administrator rights is not enough.

An existing device management provider can instead allowlist this app for lock task mode. See the managed kiosk guide in the project documentation.

Use Exit kiosk in settings to leave lockdown. If dKiosk is the home app, choose another home app after exiting.
Managed lockdown is unavailable. Check device provisioning before using this as a public kiosk.
This turns managed lockdown off so you can leave. Turn it on again in settings before returning the device to public use.
Your device manager controls this lock task session. Ask the administrator to release it.
